r.문화권·종교: French-speaking · Catholic tradition, strict separation of church and state called laicite
r.경제 체제: Market economy · aerospace, nuclear power, luxury goods, farming, large public sector
r.경제협력체: European Union (EU), Eurozone, G7, G20, OECD
r.한국이 파는 것: Ships 45%, Cars 13%, Electronics, electrical equipment 8%, Other machinery, computers 4% (2025, share of value)
r.한국이 사는 것: Machinery, computers 13%, Aircraft 9%, Bags and leather goods 8%, Gold, precious metals, gems 6% (2025, share of value)
r.한국과 맺은 FTA: Korea-EU FTA (provisionally applied 2011, fully in force 2015)
r.정치 구도: A semi-presidential system in which a directly elected president appoints the prime minister and leads foreign and defense policy. Parliament can bring down the government with a no-confidence vote, so when the president and the parliamentary majority differ, governments are often unstable. Since the snap election of 2024, parliament has been split into three blocs, a left alliance, the center and the far-right National Rally, with no majority, and prime ministers have changed several times in a short span. Pension reform and the budget deficit are major issues.

t.why: A permanent member of the UN Security Council and a nuclear power, and a member of NATO and the G7. With Germany it is an axis of EU decisions, and it leads the argument that Europe should have security capabilities independent of the United States. It makes a large share of its electricity from nuclear power and speaks for nuclear in Europe's energy debates. It kept troops in former West African colonies for a long time but has recently withdrawn from several. It extends its cultural influence through the international organization of French-speaking countries.
t.rel: France and Germany fought each other in two world wars, but since their 1963 friendship treaty they have led European integration together. With Britain it both cooperates and clashes over migrants crossing the Channel. Most of its neighbors, including Spain, Italy and Belgium, are EU members, so people and goods move freely.
t.korea: The two first established relations with the 1886 Korea-France treaty, and France sent a battalion to the Korean War. Korea's KTX high-speed rail began with French technology, and the two compete in nuclear exports. Royal Uigwe books taken during the French campaign of 1866 returned to Korea in 2011 in the form of a loan. French luxury goods and cosmetics feature often in Korean consumer news.
t.know: Thanks to its overseas territories, France has more time zones than any other country.
etext: The world's largest companies in luxury goods such as bags, clothing, cosmetics, cognac and champagne are French. Brand value lets them avoid competing on price.

It is the heart of the European aircraft maker Airbus and strong in jet engines and defense. Because it makes most of its electricity from nuclear power, electricity is relatively cheap by European standards.
Public spending and government debt are high, and governments often wobble over how to cut the deficit. Its labor regulations are considered strict.
